data.cultural_impact: The name Shalah, in Arabic culture, represents the hope and desire for peace and calmness in family life and society as a whole. It is often given to babies born during peaceful times, symbolizing the hope that they will grow up to be agents of peace and harmony.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name Shalah carries deep spiritual significance, representing the inner peace and tranquility that comes from staying close to Allah. It is a reminder of the importance of seeking inner peace and submission to the will of Allah, and striving for calmness and serenity in times of turmoil and stress. By embodying the essence of Shalah, one can cultivate inner peace and work towards creating a peaceful and harmonious community.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 12, page 377 The name Shalah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shalah ibn Rashid Al-Aslami, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), was appointed as the governor of Kufa by Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He is known for his piety and justice during his rule. However, he was removed from his post after a false accusation.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Al-Mawāqi⁒ al-Ţabī⁒ī al-Khūūūsīyah, Volume 2, page 541 The name Shalah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shalah ibn Rukn Al-Din Al-Damishqi, a renowned scholar and historian, wrote a famous book titled 'Lisan Al-Arab' which is considered one of the most comprehensive Arabic language dictionaries. He also served as the vizier (advisor) to the Fatimid Caliph Al-Mustansir Billah.
